rows.title: Nearly 70% of Colorado land zoned for housing prohibits the most affordable types of homes, study finds
rows.standfirst: In the first comprehensive review of Colorado land use laws, the National Zoning Atlas found that you can build single-family homes almost anywhere. But apartments, condos and townhomes are widely prohibited.

rows.title: Are app-only grocery store coupons illegal in Colorado?
rows.standfirst: No. Despite complaints that digital and app-only coupons exclude some shoppers, there are no federal or state laws against them.

rows.title: A Colorado trucking school is trying to train drivers to handle the unique challenges of mountain driving
rows.standfirst: According to the Colorado Department of Transportation, each hour I-70 is closed results in an estimated economic loss of more than $1 million and those impacts can extend 100 miles or more

rows.title: Safeway workers end three-week strike after union, grocer reach tentative contract agreement
rows.standfirst: United Food & Commercial Workers Local 7, which represents Safeway workers, said the contract must still be ratified by its members

rows.title: Wolves are killing cattle in Colorado. Feeling cut off from wildlife officials, ranchers seek their own solution.
rows.standfirst: Western slope ranchers are organizing to seek a resolution to their wolf problem. Is receiving payment to live with the wolves the answer?

rows.title: Cañon City’s Main Street makeover is eating into peak tourist season. But there’s light at the end of the tunnel.
rows.standfirst: Shops and restaurants say they’re hanging on as best they can while the city nears the final stretch of improvements to make the longest historic Main Street in the state more appealing

rows.title: Nederland to buy Eldora Mountain Resort with support of ski industry heavy hitters
rows.standfirst: The purchase of Eldora will be funded by bonds to be paid off using lift-ticket and other on-mountain revenue rather than Nederland taxes

rows.title: What’s Working: Nonprofit thrift store is training technicians to service Colorado’s electric vehicle charging stations
rows.standfirst: Goodwill of Colorado has a mission to help the down-and-out find jobs and careers. Plus: Colorado gets back $36 million in frozen federal EV funds

rows.title: Colorado’s property insurer of last resort is now covering more than two dozen families
rows.standfirst: The Fair Access to Insurance Requirements Plan, or FAIR Plan, began accepting applications from residential property owners on April 10

rows.title: Colorado’s housing crisis won’t be fixed by zoning alone. A new report shows why.
rows.standfirst: Advocates launched a new housing consortium in March that hopes to tackle the dizzying array of factors that drive up housing costs

rows.title: Jared Polis’ plan to mitigate the economic impact of Trump’s next tariffs? Track the data.
rows.standfirst: On-again, off-again tariffs have Colorado companies wondering what will really happen Aug. 1, when taxes on goods from Canada and Mexico go into effect.

rows.title: Want to buy an electric vehicle in Colorado? Do it now, before tax credits expire.
rows.standfirst: A $7,500 federal tax credit expires Sept. 30, and Colorado’s own credit plummets Jan. 1. Now is the time to go electric if you can swing it.

rows.title: What’s Working: Colorado global exports are up, imports are down amid tariff roller coaster
rows.standfirst: New tariffs are scheduled to start August 1. Plus: What 2,333 Coloradans think about the economy, June unemployment and jobs report, more!

rows.title: Saving Kit Carson: Inside one rural Colorado town’s battle to stay alive and revitalize its community
rows.standfirst: Faced with declining population, a housing shortage and flagging economic fortunes, locals — including a returning son — have stepped up

rows.title: The number of people starting a Colorado business jumped 19% from a year ago
rows.standfirst: That was a surprise increase and could be a sign some residents are confident about their startup prospects or need an additional income, state officials say

rows.title: Durango’s Farm to Summit turns bruised, cosmetically flawed local crops into gourmet meals for backpackers
rows.standfirst: The 3-year-old company recently received a $250,000 grant from the state, enabling it to expand and open a new production facility in Durango

rows.title: Trump v. Colorado: How the president’s energy agenda is clashing with the state’s lofty green ambitions
rows.standfirst: The Trump administration has already cut off federal subsidies and prioritized fossil fuel initiatives, threatening to push the state even further behind in its energy goals

rows.title: Building new gas power plants would mean higher energy bills. Here’s how the math works.
rows.standfirst: Even after federal tax credits for clean energy development were erased, it’s still more expensive to build new “dispatchable” electric plants

rows.title: Has cannabis generated more than $2.5B in sales tax revenue for Colorado?
rows.standfirst: Yes. Cannabis sales have raised almost $3 billion in tax revenue for Colorado since the state began taxing the drug, state data shows.

rows.title: Starlink, Amazon asking for $300M of Colorado’s broadband money after federal rule changes
rows.standfirst: After the Trump administration changed the rules last month to prioritize the cheapest proposals, the state’s effort to award $826.5 million to ISPs to build infrastructure had to start over. Fiber took a back seat.

rows.title: USDA to scatter half its Washington staff to field offices, including Fort Collins. Critics see a ploy to cut jobs.
rows.standfirst: USDA lost 15,000 people earlier this year. Some worry this plan will further weaken research, services for farmers and rural Americans.

rows.title: What’s Working: AI skills aren’t just for tech workers anymore, even in Colorado
rows.standfirst: In a study by Lightcast, 51% of AI-related job listings were outside typical tech roles. A Denver tech-education company is capturing that data and building it into its course offerings.

rows.title: Women have filed more than 60% of Colorado’s paid family and medical leave insurance claims
rows.standfirst: Most Colorado workers, including the self-employed, are eligible for paid time off. Most who have taken it are caring for themselves during leave.

rows.title: Is 3D printing the future of building houses? This Colorado company hopes to cement the model.
rows.standfirst: VeroTouch, based in Salida, was the first to 3D print homes in Colorado. The company is developing a community in the high country it hopes can be a model for other rural areas.

rows.title: Xcel gets OK to spend $30M to join short-term wholesale market, despite limited benefits
rows.standfirst: Markets+ aims to lower bills and increase grid reliability, but Xcel is limiting its participation
